title: The Fox Borrows the Tiger's Might
text:
King Xuan of Chu once asked his ministers why the states to the north were so afraid of his general Zhao Xixu. One of them, Jiang Yi, answered with a story.

A tiger hunting for food caught a fox. Before it could eat him, the fox said: "You dare not eat me. The Lord of Heaven has made me the leader of all the animals. If you eat me, you defy his command. If you don't believe me, walk behind me and see whether any animal fails to run when I appear."

The tiger agreed and followed the fox through the forest. Every creature that saw them fled in panic. The tiger, not realizing that it was he whom they feared, believed the fox.

Jiang Yi then made his point. The king's realm was five thousand li across and his armies numbered a million men, and he had placed them under Zhao Xixu. The northern states, he said, did not fear the general. They feared the king's own armed might, just as the animals feared the tiger and not the fox.
lesson: When people defer to someone who reports to you, check whether they respect that person or only the power you lent them. And if you are the fox, remember whose strength you are walking with.
people: Jiang Yi, King Xuan of Chu, Zhao Xixu
source: Zhanguo Ce (Strategies of the Warring States), Chu
